title: Optimal Average Success Probabilities of Binary $(n,n-1)$ and $(n,n-2)$ Quantum Random Access Codes via a Proof of the Corresponding Conjectured Bound
abstract: A binary $(n,m)$ quantum random access code (QRAC) compresses an $n$-bit classical string into an $m$-qubit quantum state, from which a decoder attempts to recover a randomly selected target bit. Of particular interest is the optimal average probability of success, $P^{Q,\mathrm{avg},\mathrm{opt}}_{n,m}$, which is numerically conjectured to satisfy the bound $P^{Q,\mathrm{avg},\mathrm{opt}}_{n,m}\leq \frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{\frac{m}{n}}$. Recent constructions of $(n,n-1)$ QRACs by Suzuki and $(n,n-2)$ QRACs by Akibue et al. meet this bound exactly, raising the question of their strict optimality. In this work, we settle this question by proving the conjectured upper bound for $m\in\{n-1,n-2\}$, thereby precisely determining $P^{Q,\mathrm{avg},\mathrm{opt}}_{n,n-1}$ and $P^{Q,\mathrm{avg},\mathrm{opt}}_{n,n-2}$. The proof utilizes a translation recently studied by Lin and de Wolf from local to global reconstruction via pretty good measurement, along with dimensional and positive-semidefinite constraints on an induced channel.
summary: This paper rigorously determines the maximum achievable average success probability for specific types of Quantum Random Access Codes (QRACs). By proving a long-standing conjectured upper bound using advanced techniques involving Pretty Good Measurement, the authors precisely characterize the optimal performance limits for $(n, n-1)$ and $(n, n-2)$ QRACs.
main_problem: The primary goal is determining the optimal average success probability for binary Quantum Random Access Codes (QRACs).
main_result: The authors prove that the conjectured upper bound, $P^{Q,\mathrm{avg},\mathrm{opt}}_{n,m}\leq  rac{1}{2}+ rac{1}{2}\sqrt{ rac{m}{n}}$, is indeed the exact optimal probability for the specific cases where $m=n-1$ and $m=n-2$.
method: The proof employs advanced techniques involving translating local reconstruction problems to global ones via Pretty Good Measurement (PGM) and utilizing positive-semidefinite constraints on induced quantum channels.
model_or_system: The model is the binary $(n, m)$ Quantum Random Access Code (QRAC), which encodes an $n$-bit classical string into an $m$-qubit quantum state for subsequent decoding.
key_observables: Average Success Probability ($P^C$), coordinate-wise success probability ($p^C_i$), and the expected Hamming distance ($\Delta_{C,PGM}$) after PGM.
main_assumptions: The proof relies on established results concerning the reduction from local to global reconstruction via Pretty Good Measurement (PGM) studied by Lin and de Wolf.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the problem definition, introduces the conjectured bound, and then proceeds through technical lemmas (related to PGM and positive-semidefinite constraints) culminating in a theorem that proves the upper bound for $m \in \{n-1, n-2\}$.
why_interesting: While focused on QRACs, the mathematical techniques involving channel analysis, bounds derived from semidefinite programming, and information theoretic limits are highly relevant to understanding error correction and quantum communication protocols.
